body.text: In short:
Technology giant Nvidia is initiating an investigation into a report CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
Mr Huang has admitted to staff he had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
What's next?
Nvidia says the investigation will be overseen by independent directors and legal counsel, and Mr Huang will remain in his role.

Technology giant and artificial chip manufacturer Nvidia says it is launching an independent investigation after a media report that its founder and CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Top Republican members of Congress in the US House of Representatives have called on Mr Huang to brief Congress this month about a New York Times report in October alleging he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.
The media outlet reported last month that US authorities were investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia.

Nvidia said on Sunday, local time, that while its board had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information.
"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," a statement said.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
Mr Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, the company said.

US President Donald Trump said he had not yet spoken to Mr Huang about the allegations despite the pair maintaining a close relationship. Speaking to reporters in Florida on Sunday evening, Mr Trump said the NVIDIA CEO was a "fine person" who had done an "incredible job".

Asked if he should have acted on intelligence suggesting Mr Huang had been compromised when he was briefed roughly a year ago, according to the New York Times, Mr Trump did not directly comment, instead choosing to heap more praise on the embattled executive.
"I think he's an honourable guy, I think he probably has an excuse for it," he said.
"He's done an amazing job for our country."
Axios reported on Sunday, citing a draft email by Mr Huang to employees, that he admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions.
"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Mr Huang said in the draft email seen by Reuters.

Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, Mr Huang said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
An Nvidia spokesperson said Mr Huang was "committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption."
Jensen Huang's memo to staff
I owe my family and all of you an apology.
I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.

Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.
To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.
To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me.

Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.

Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.
My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.
Jensen Huang
Source: Bloomberg
Who is Jensen Huang?
Mr Huang is a central figure in the global push toward AI development, and has forced a close working relationship with United States President Donald Trump.
He has previously encouraged the White House to lift restrictions on the sale of advanced AI chips to China, arguing the measures accelerate Beijing's own development of the technology.
Nvidia is valued at about $US5.4 trillion ($7.7 trillion), making it the world's most valuable company as demand for AI hardware and data centres has skyrocketed.
Mr Huang was born in Taiwan and raised in Thailand before he emigrated alone to the US to attend a boarding school at the age of 10.
He has previously described AI as the world's next industrial revolution and argues that whichever country has its technology adopted the most worldwide will win the AI race.
ABC/Reuters
